rationale: From the available tool-call record, the agent appears to have: (1) authenticated the user (find_user_id_by_name_zip, get_user_details) and pulled order details; but then (2) executed modify_pending_order_items (twice, with different parameters) without any clear, prior user confirmation shown; and (3) executed modify_user_address even though the user only wanted the address changed if partial cancellation was not possible. Performing both a partial cancellation and an address change conflicts with the user’s conditional request. There is also no evidence the agent computed and communicated the total refund amount or confirmed refund to the original payment method before or after making changes. Given policy requirements to confirm before any order-changing write and to act only per the user’s conditional instructions, this interaction does not meet the pass bar. Confidence is moderate due to incomplete visibility into the conversation text, but the tool-call pattern strongly suggests policy violations.
